lines.text: 'To show the beldam daughters of her daughter,
lines.meaning: Time lets a grandmother live to see her granddaughters.
lines.why: "Beldam" is an old word for grandmother (it later came to mean "hag"), and "the daughters of her daughter" are her granddaughters. So Time shows the old woman the children of her own daughter, and it is Time that lets one generation follow another.

lines.text: To make the child a man, the man a child,
lines.meaning: Time turns children into men, and later turns old men back into helpless children.

lines.text: To slay the tiger that doth live by slaughter,
lines.meaning: Time kills even the tiger, which lives by killing.

lines.text: To tame the unicorn and lion wild,
lines.meaning: Time tames the fiercest beasts, the unicorn and the wild lion.
lines.why: The unicorn was believed to be fierce and untamable, and the lion was the emblem of savagery and royal power.

lines.text: To mock the subtle in themselves beguiled,
lines.meaning: Time makes fools of clever people by letting them be tricked by their own scheming.
lines.why: "Subtle" is used here as a noun for crafty, scheming people. "Beguiled" means deceived, and "in themselves" means by their own doing, so these are people who have fooled themselves. "Mock" is what Time does to them. It exposes them as dupes of their own cunning.
lines.example: A con man so taken with his own lies that they end up ruining him.

lines.text: To cheer the ploughman with increaseful crops,
lines.meaning: Time cheers the ploughman (farmer) with plentiful (increaseful) crops.

lines.text: And waste huge stones with little water drops.
lines.meaning: And Time wears away (wastes) huge stones with nothing more than small drops of water.
lines.why: This is the old saying that constant dripping hollows out a stone.

summary: It is Time's job to let a grandmother live to see her granddaughters, to turn children into men and later turn old men back into helpless children, to kill the tiger that lives by killing and tame the unicorn and the wild lion, to make fools of the cunning by letting their own schemes trick them, to cheer the farmer with plentiful crops, and to wear away huge stones with nothing but small drops of water.
